releases.name: HashRing.add_nodes
releases.body:
Merge #2 
Rebuilding the ring each time the ring changes turns out to be a really slow operation. This hopes to address this by creating an `add_nodes` operation that can be performed on an empty ring that is faster than individually calling `add_node` for each node in the ring. So far, the benchmarks are promising, the `add_nodes` operation taking 2% the wall time of calling `add_node` individually for larger ring sizes. Right now, this operation will run in the event loop of our API servers, so making it go faster is a good way to reduce the impact of re-building the ring.

Here is a result of the benches of adding nodes in the slow (add_node) vs fast (add_nodes) path, for 512 replicas per node:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5489149/35601571-a3f5e65c-05e8-11e8-8b31-caceb908f56d.png)


 - [x] add `HashRing.add_nodes(nodes)` method.
 - [x] add `HashRing.get_num_items()` method for debugging.
 - [x] add `HashRing.get_node(node_name)` method for debugging. 
 - [x] add `hash_ring_sort` method that will sort the ring items array after we're done adding stuff to 
it.
 - [x] add `hash_ring_ensure_items_size` which will allow us to pre-allocate the `items` array, so we do not need to needlessly realloc it to grow, if we can compute the target size before hand.
 - [x] mod `hash_ring_add_node` to take a `doSort` param, to defer sorting of the items array. 
 - [x] formalize benchmarks with pytest-bench
 - [x] test coverage around this.

pullRequests.title: [windows] Fix compiler error against MSVC
pullRequests.body:
Error was:
```
contrib/sort.c(52): error C2057: expected constant expression
contrib/sort.c(52): error C2466: cannot allocate an array of constant size 0
contrib/sort.c(52): error C2133: 'starts': unknown size
contrib/sort.c(52): error C2133: 'ends': unknown size
```

Opted to use a macro constant rather than a static int...

pullRequests.title: Make version requirement for six loose
pullRequests.body: Exact version pins are bad, worse when in a library, and even worse when for a common dependency like six.

pullRequests.title: Some small fixups
pullRequests.body:
* Re-comment out the pytest requirements, this causes weird issues in
  our upstream virtualenv since this ends up wanting to install latest
  pytest but we have older versions pinned and end up upgrading then
  downgrading every time due to this disagreement on version
* Mark the generated c file as generated to ease future diffs in github
